They rank; they fetch nothing. Only fux answer can raise it -- that is the whole difference between the two verbs.
fux lexical is this pipeline with the graph tier, the mined fold and the intent prior forced off -- and it is FROZEN.
It is the baseline every ranking verdict and the Python/Node differential law compare against (SR-CLI decision 12). ask = lexical, then the tier.

THE SAME PATH, IN THE NODE READER
.fux/node/fux.mjs runs this pipeline exactly -- same analyzer and families, same guard, same BM25F + anchor, same mined fold, intent prior, pin, graph tier,
sort key and band -- and it reads tune.toml and output.toml, so a tuned repo ranks the same. Scores equal after round(9); the order has no tolerance.
--fast reads .fux/runtime/ when the plane is fresh (W-242 Tier 1, alpha.10) and `fux build` rebuilds it byte-identically (Tier 2), so ranked_by says accelerator or scan truthfully on both readers.
The one asymmetry is the graph tier: Python needs a fresh graph.json or has no tier; Node reads it when fresh and otherwise rebuilds the plane in memory (W-259), so Node never
requires fux build. Node never fetches and has no decoder plane -- neither matters here, because ask fetches nothing.

Drawn from the code, 2026-10-05. src/fux/cli.py, src/fux/api.py, src/fux/query/*.py, src/fux/derive/accel.py, src/fux/templates/tune.toml.txt + output.toml.txt, src/fux/constants.toml, node/src/query/run.mjs.
